items.prose: A pairs book earns 1.20% a month before a break in its pairs and 0.54% after.
items.question: What share of the return survived?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Divide after by before.

byKey.pts: That is the fall in points a month.

items.prose: After a strategy is published, fewer of its pairs reach 2 sd and gains per trade shrink. The share of opened trades that close at a crossing holds at 75%.
items.question: Which story fits best?

options.text: Crowding: others close the gaps sooner

options.why: Broken pairs open and fail to converge. Here convergence held at 75%.
Fewer opens and smaller gains together are a pattern, not noise.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Ask what each story does to convergence.

explain.text: Crowding shrinks and pre-empts gaps but leaves trades converging. Broken pairs would cut the crossing share, which held. So the evidence points at crowding here.

items.prose: A pairs book runs two cycles. The first opens 40 trades and 26 close at a crossing. The second opens 50 and 25 do.
items.question: What is the convergence share over both cycles?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Pool the trades: total crossings over total trades.

byKey.avg: You averaged the two shares, 65% and 50%. Pool the trades instead.

explain.text: 51 crossings in 90 trades is 56.7%. Averaging the two cycle shares gives 57.5%, which weights the smaller cycle too heavily.

items.prose: A researcher tests the 190 pairs within one sector for cointegration at 5%. Suppose none is cointegrated.
items.question: How many pairs pass by chance on average?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Multiply the tests by the level.

byKey.one: That is the chance for one test.

explain.text: 190 × 0.05 = 9.5 chance passes, even with no real pair among them.

items.prose: Fund L doubles the daily moves of index A. So ln L moves twice as far as ln A, plus a stationary gap.
items.question: Which rule can select the pair L and A?

options.text: Engle-Granger, with a hedge ratio near 2
Distance, if the formation year is calm
options.why: Distance fixes a 1 to 1 hedge. Doubled moves pull the normalised prices apart in any year.

options.text: Both, since the gap is stationary
options.why: Only the rule that estimates the slope sees the stationary gap.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Which rule estimates the hedge ratio?

explain.text: Engle-Granger regresses ln L on ln A and finds a slope near 2 with a stationary residual. Distance compares normalised prices, which drift apart. On our panel such a pair ranked 177th by distance.

items.prose: At start 0, Engle-Granger choosing from the 50 closest pairs keeps 10 chance pairs with p-values below 0.01. Distance's top 20 are all planted.
items.question: What explains the chance pairs?

options.text: Fifty tests on one year of noisy closes: some chance pairs score low, and some planted pairs score high
Those chance pairs are really cointegrated
options.why: They are independent random walks by construction.

options.text: Engle-Granger cannot detect a half-life of 8 days
options.why: Most planted pairs do pass; five of the 20 fail at 5%.

options.text: Distance and Engle-Granger always agree on the best pairs
options.why: They measure different things and disagree often.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Think about many tests on a short, noisy sample.

explain.text: Fifty tests give chance passes, and a year of closes with a bounce is a short, noisy sample. Five planted pairs fail at 5%, while some chance pairs score near zero. A low p-value from one year is weak evidence.

items.prose: A regression of 22 cycle returns on the market gives α = 0.0623 and β = 0.0529 a cycle.
items.question: What does the line predict for a cycle in which the market rises 15%?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Alpha plus beta times the market's return.

explain.text: 0.0623 + 0.0529 × 0.15 = 0.0702. The market adds under a point; almost all the return is alpha.

items.prose: Both shares load 1 on their industry factor. A cointegration hedge goes long £1 of A and short £1.25 of B.
items.question: What is the net industry exposure, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Long exposure minus short exposure.

byKey.pos: The short leg is larger, so the net is negative.

explain.text: £1 − £1.25 = −£0.25. The position is net short a quarter of a pound of the industry factor.

items.prose: A sweep of 12 settings runs on years 1 to 6. The best is then run on years 7 to 12. A colleague also reruns all 12 on years 7 to 12.
items.question: Which figure is out of sample?

options.text: The years 7 to 12 return of the setting chosen on years 1 to 6
The best of the 12 settings on years 7 to 12
options.why: Choosing on the held-out years makes them in sample.

options.text: The best setting's years 1 to 6 return
options.why: That is in sample by definition.

options.text: The average of all 12 on years 7 to 12
options.why: No single rule earned that average, so it reports no strategy.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Out of sample means chosen before the look.

explain.text: Only a setting fixed before the held-out years open gives an out-of-sample figure. The best held-out cell is a best-of-12 on those years.

items.prose: A held-out run earns −0.03% a month against 1.20% in sample. The note's survival line comes from `survival_sentence(pre, post)`.
items.question: What should the line read?

options.why: A negative share is reported as none surviving.
The result is clear on this test: nothing survived.
Over 100% was lost; the line says none survived.

feedback.generic: Not quite. A ratio at or below zero reads none.

explain.text: −0.03 / 1.20 is negative, so nothing survived. The note says so with the same prominence as a success.
